question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $13,$ the additive inverse of $39$ modulo $13$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $39$ modulo $13$ is the integer $0\le x<13$ such that

$$
x+39≡0\,(\text{mod}\,13).
$$

First, note that $39≡3\cdot 13≡0\,(\text{mod}\,13),$ and $0+0≡0\,(\text{mod}\,13).$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $39$ modulo $13$ is $0.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
39+0≡3\cdot 13+0≡3\cdot 0+0≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,13)
$$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
